title: fix: classify upstream timeouts and name common errors
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Report upstream 408 timeouts as 504 while retaining the original upstream status and error body.
- Preserve the existing no-fallback rule after Portkey exhausts our 290-second deadline.
- Add missing machine-readable codes and messages for 408, 410, 413, 426, and 504.
- Tests: 90 status, provider-client, fallback, and error-observability tests; gen typecheck passes.

gist.headline: Timeouts get proper names
gist.blurb: When an upstream provider runs out the clock, the hive now labels the situation correctly instead of leaving everyone to interpret a mysterious 408. The original provider status and error body still make it home intact.
gist.summary: Upstream 408 timeouts are now returned as 504 responses while preserving the original upstream status and error body, and shared machine-readable error codes/messages now cover 408, 410, 413, 426, and 504 without changing the 290-second Portkey no-fallback rule.
gist.impact: API clients can reliably recognize gateway timeouts as 504 and handle five common HTTP failures through stable error codes while retaining upstream debugging details.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy API garden has a rain-soaked upstream clocktower marked 408 handing Polli a clearly labeled 504 parcel, while a retro terminal preserves a tiny original-error note. Polli, wearing a miniature mail carrier cap, calmly sorts the named error packets beside code-plants; the scene represents accurate timeout classification without losing diagnostic context.
